channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Proposed 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule: What PTs Need to Know, Part 1
item.description: The U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services estimates that physical therapy codes could see an overall payment increase of 1-3% under the Calendar Year 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Proposed Rule, despite a proposed 1.68% decrease to the conversion factor.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Fake podiatrist sentence to be served in the community
item.description: A fake podiatrist in Australia was sentenced to community service, highlighting the role of the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) in managing health practitioner registration.
item.author: AHPRA

item.title: Clinical practice guideline for physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty: revision 2026.
item.description: The American Physical Therapy Association is updating its clinical practice guideline for total knee arthroplasty, with the revision scheduled for 2026. This guideline, developed by a multidisciplinary group and based on a systematic review, includes 20 recommendations addressing benefits, harms, feasibility, and patient preferences.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative efficacy of different joint mobilization techniques in shoulder adhesive capsulitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the clinical effects of different non-thrust joint mobilization approaches for shoulder adhesive capsulitis, analyzing English-language RCTs published between 2000 and 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Advocates, Leaders Drive Payment Momentum During APTA Payment Advocacy Summit
item.description: The APTA Payment Advocacy Summit gathered 450 advocates to build on recent state payment wins in 2025-2026, emphasizing the association's top priority: advancing payment for physical therapist services.
item.author: APTA

item.title: APTA Members Unite to Advance Payment Advocacy Via New SPARC Forum and Pledge
item.description: APTA introduced the new SPARC Forum and the APTA Payment Advocacy Pledge to empower members to drive meaningful payment reform and strengthen the future of the profession.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Beyond "Biomedical-Plus": Reclaiming the biopsychosocial model in musculoskeletal physiotherapy.
item.description: The biopsychosocial (BPS) model is often reduced to "biomedical-plus" in MSK physiotherapy. This article argues for a more authentic BPS application through professional Confidence, role Clarity, and Compassionate communication.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Combined Biopsychosocial Interventions for Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found combined biopsychosocial interventions significantly reduce pain and functional disability in adults with chronic low back pain (≥12 weeks) compared to usual care or unimodal interventions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Cost-effectiveness of stratified physiotherapy integrated with digital health versus usual physiotherapy for neck and/or shoulder pain: results of a cluster randomised clinical trial.
item.description: A cluster randomized clinical trial found that a Stratified Blended Physiotherapy Approach (SBPA), integrating prognostic risk stratification with digital health, was cost-effective compared to usual physiotherapy for 136 patients with neck and/or shoulder pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of an individualised swimming and education programme for chronic low back pain (EduSwim): a randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An individualized swimming and education program, delivered via telehealth, significantly improved disability in adults with chronic non-specific low back pain at 8 weeks compared to education alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual Reality-assisted Physiotherapeutic Training for Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 RCTs found that virtual reality-assisted physiotherapy significantly improved pain (SMD = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.14-0.65), physical function (SMD = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.05-0.70), and balance (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.16-0.72) in patients with knee osteoarthritis compared to traditional rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: In adult patients with brainstem strokes, does dysphagia rehabilitation improve health-related outcomes compared to usual care for inpatients? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies (n=443 participants) explored the effectiveness of dysphagia rehabilitation on swallow function in adult inpatients with brainstem stroke, categorizing interventions into traditional swallowing therapy or device inclusion.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of different modes of digital health interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of different modes of digital health interventions for sarcopenia in older adults, addressing sarcopenia-related disability as a public health challenge.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Outpatient rehabilitation can prevent suicide after acquired brain injury.
item.description: A registry study (n=591 treated patients, n=2,932 controls) suggests that outpatient rehabilitation may prevent suicide after acquired brain injury, with a higher suicide frequency found in general population post-stroke and TBI.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A systematic review of current evidence on clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques in sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
item.description: This systematic review aims to evaluate the clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques for sacroiliac joint dysfunction (SIJD), with studies published between January 2021 and December 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploring equity in telehealth interventions in physiotherapy: A meta-epidemiological study.
item.description: A meta-epidemiological study (n=94 telehealth equity trials) assessed equity in physiotherapy telehealth interventions using the PROGRESS Plus framework, identifying gaps in reaching vulnerable populations.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Responsiveness of the Arabic version of the lower extremity functional scale in individuals with lower extremity musculoskeletal disorders.
item.description: This study examined the responsiveness of the Arabic version of the Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) in 74 individuals with lower extremity musculoskeletal disorders. LEFS change scores showed good correlation with other outcome measures, supporting its utility in clinical practice.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence to exercise intervention including pain threshold, exercise and physiotherapy sessions for patients with chronic rotator cuff tendinopathy.
item.description: This study investigated adherence to two pain threshold protocols during a 26-week exercise intervention for 84 patients with chronic rotator cuff tendinopathy, analyzing secondary data from an RCT with 1-year follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Research progress on horticultural therapy in patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment: a narrative review.
item.description: This narrative review evaluated horticultural therapy (HT) for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), finding it significantly improves memory, executive function, and orientation, and categorized HT protocols into five types.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Association of Depression, Anxiety, and Quality of Life with Sexual Function in Young-to-Middle-Aged Stroke Patients: A Case-Control Study.
item.description: This case-control study (n=60) found young-to-middle-aged stroke patients had significantly higher Arizona Sexual Experience Scale scores (19.3 ± 6.6 vs. 13.0 ± 3.1, p < 0.001) and greater sexual dysfunction prevalence than controls, with a significant decline in sexual satisfaction.
item.author: PubMed
